title: A Lean-checked one-step theorem and an independent re-check of 2.8 million steps of a validated enclosure of Robertson's problem
description:
A validated enclosure of Robertson's stiff problem on [0,4000] (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24216837) had its key step theorem argued in prose. We state and prove that theorem in Lean 4 for Robertson's reduced system (midpoint identity, one-sided Grönwall bound for any sign of the constant, tube invariance by clamping, existence, uniqueness, chaining with the exact 2x2 spectral norm, gluing of two pieces; strict gate: compilation, per-theorem axiom report, axioms restricted to propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, no sorry), and we write a second implementation, an independent checker in Rust with Arb, that recomputes the theorems' numerical hypotheses from exact per-step records. All 2,843,424 steps of the regenerated run are certified in one streaming pass (6 h 21 min, 5.6 MB of checker memory); the checker's final boxes for (y2, y3) lie inside the stored checkpoint enclosures, which lie inside the published ones. After t = 400 the checker's bound is much tighter than the producer's (factor 7 at t = 1000, 18 at t = 4000); we give evidence, from two record windows, a 281-point sample of t <= 1000 and the producer's source, that this comes from interval division of a wide logarithmic-norm ball in the producer at occasional steps and not from optimism in the checker; the range 1000 < t <= 4000 was not examined finely.

Scope and limits. Tier C. There is no Lean theorem for the whole chain: the theorems cover a step, the chaining between two steps and the gluing of two pieces; the induction over the steps lives in the checker's code. The checker is unverified Rust code; Arb, FLINT, GMP and MPFR are assumed correct; the link between the checker's arithmetic and the Lean hypotheses is a reviewed correspondence, not a proof (the tube-radius rule, box enclosure, closed-form eigenvalue and defect bound are the checker's own derivations). Mutation tests of the checker's source, reported in the paper, show that two of four one-line mutations are not rejected by the checker's own gates in the headline mode (an optimistic constant is caught only by comparison with the producer's values). The Robertson field and Jacobian are hard-coded in the checker; an independent AI audit found them identical to the Lean ones, the human comparison is owed; no human has reviewed the Lean statements. AI-generated under human direction; one independent AI audit by a model of the same family (ACCEPT_WITH_CORRECTIONS, all corrections applied; AUDIT.md and AUDIT_RESPONSE.md in the bundle); not peer reviewed. The bundle contains the Lean files, the checker source, preregistrations, run logs, stream hashes, mutation controls and diagnostic scripts, with a sha256 manifest.
notes: Preprint v1 (2026-11-25). AI-generated under human direction (Anthropic Claude models); independently AI-audited once by a model of the same family (AUDIT.md and AUDIT_RESPONSE.md in the evidence bundle); not peer reviewed; no human review of the Lean statements. Tier C.
